spaces.title: Art Wall
spaces.description: Located directly above the Ask Us service point, the Art Wall welcomes you to Level 2 of the Hunt Library and is highly visible throughout the Rain Garden Reading Lounge. At night, it is even visible from outside the building on The Oval. The Art Wall showcases student, faculty, staff, and community art and design projects. See below for how to contact us about displaying your work. Have a content idea? If you are interested in exhibiting your work on the Art Wall, fill out this form or send a description of your idea to the Libraries' Director of Communications, Chris Tonelli, at catonell@ncsu.edu .

photo.alt: Two students talking in front of the Hunt Art Wall that is mounted above the Ask us desk.

spaces.title: Ask Us
spaces.description: The Hunt Library's one-stop service center, where staff are ready to help you. What can I do here? Have a question? Need to find a room, book, or piece of software? Our friendly staff can help! Just ask us. Borrow technology . We lend everything from calculators and charging cables to synthesizers. Borrow books including textbooks . Pick up interlibrary loan requests.

spaces.title: Audio Rooms
spaces.description: Audio Rooms are fully equipped for creating and mixing music, recording voiceovers, transferring audio from analog formats, and editing digital media. If you are seeking a traditional piano experience, there are eight practice studios available to NC State students on a first-come, f irst-served basis in Price Music Center, the home of the Music Department. You must complete an online orientation before reserving an Audio Room. Note that it will take up to 48 hours for you to be added to the system; if you need a reservation on the same day you take the orientation please stop by the space and ask for help from a consultant. You will need to complete the orientation in both cases, but we may be able to set you up with a reservation same day if you stop by in person. The Media Spaces at Hunt are staffed during our open hours . You can find drop-in consultation assistance for projects, technology, and more just by stopping by.

photo.alt: 2 people sitting in an audio room, with one playing guitar and the other singing.

spaces.title: Auditorium
spaces.description: The Auditorium provides for panel discussions, HD capture and video conferencing sessions, and special presentations like roundtables and mini forums. The audiovisual system includes an extended desktop display solution enabling multiple images to be projected on the projection screen. A sample of equipment in the room includes: two HD DLP projectors, multi-windowing video processor, blu-ray player and auxiliary AV inputs, program audio and movie surround sound system, color touch panel with source device preview and lighting control, and three HD cameras and associated mics for videoconferencing.

spaces.title: Dataspace
spaces.description: The Dataspace is one of two NC State University Libraries’ Data Labs. It provides a place for members of the NC State University community to access essential technology for working with data, including powerful computers and specialized software. The Dataspace supports anyone at NC State University working with data , creating visualizations , or using geospatial tools and methodologies . Data Science Consulting is also available in the Dataspace for help with a wide range of data topics. Consulting is typically available on weekdays when class is in session from 10am-6pm. Please visit Get Data Help for more information and details about the current schedule. The Libraries supports a community in the Dataspace that provides a conducive environment for those working with data. View community guidelines Looking for a Data Lab in Hill Library? See more about the Data Experience Lab . Explore data science services Computing Reserve a Dataspace Workstation Select "Hunt" for the building. Then select "Data Stations." If you need to make a reservation longer than four hours, please contact us. Software View list of software If you don't see a specific software that you would like to use, you may submit a Software Request .

spaces.title: Emerging Issues Commons
spaces.description: The Emerging Issues Commons is a civic engagement space designed to connect people with information to inspire action for a prosperous North Carolina. Throughout its many sections, visitors are able to hear directly from fellow North Carolinians about issues that transcend the boundaries of geography, sector, demographics and ideology. The commons is managed by the Institute for Emerging Issues, a non-partisan “Connect. Think and Do” tank committed to bringing North Carolinians together to find solutions to the state’s emerging and critical policy issues.

spaces.description: These meeting rooms are not run by the NC State Libraries. They are under the Institute for Emerging Issues (IEI) which is housed in the Hunt Library building. You can request a reservation through the IEI Request Form .

spaces.title: Idea Alcove
spaces.description: The Idea Alcove is an open, informal collaboration space, located near the Quiet Reading Room, for when consultations need to happen on the fly. This space has easily moveable furniture and a whiteboard that takes up the entire north wall.

spaces.title: Interfaith Prayer & Meditation Room
spaces.description: NC State’s interfaith prayer & meditation rooms are meant to serve and support all students and the holistic wellness of the university community, as scientific evidence demonstrates the significant cognitive and physiological benefits of meditation. The spaces allow individuals of all religious faiths and non-religious beliefs to experience a place for peace, prayer, meditation and/or reflection throughout the day. The spaces are intended for individual use and not for any organized group activity or meetings. The interfaith prayer and meditation rooms are not reservable and are available for individual students to use whenever the campus building is open. Other interfaith prayer and meditation spaces on campus

photo.alt: Open room with yellow carpet, whiteboard walls, and prayer rug.

spaces.title: iPearl Immersion Theater
spaces.description: The iPearl Immersion Theater features a nearly 20-foot-long video display with a gentle curve that immerses the viewer. Prominently located in a high-traffic area next to the Ask Us service point, the Theater is Hunt’s premiere digital exhibit space, highlighting the innovative work of NC State’s students, faculty, and staff. You can explore a variety of exhibitions by selecting them on the touch panel next to the display wall. Have a content idea? The iPearl Immersion Theater showcases a wide variety of student, faculty, staff, and community projects. If you would like to exhibit your work in the Theater, please fill out this form or send a description of your idea to Chris Tonelli, Director of Libraries Communications, at catonell@ncsu.edu .

photo.alt: Stools in front of the large, curved screen of the Immersion Theater. The screen shows visuals from an exhibit called "Hypnotizing Math."

spaces.title: Jay Lawrence and Ella Apple Technology Showcase
spaces.description: The Jay Lawrence and Ella Apple Technology Showcase at the James B. Hunt Jr. Library on Centennial Campus serves as a co-work and study space for students, and as a hub of interdisciplinary technology and craft based activities to promote and support innovation in high impact experiential learning. The Technology Showcase is a site that also hosts a variety of pop-ups, workshops, and events designed to engage Hunt Library patrons through low-stakes, playful, and engaging learning opportunities. The Fall 2026 semester is bringing several pop-up workshops presented by Libraries partners, and The Studios . In addition to various technologies, such as synthesizers, and a VR headset that libraries’ patrons can explore, an upcoming small scale materials library in collaboration with the Wilson College of Textiles will be coming to the space this Fall semester.

spaces.title: Lenovo Esports and Gaming Lab
spaces.description: The Lenovo Esports and Gaming Lab is located on the fourth floor of the Hunt Library. The NC State community can experience the thrill of competitive gaming, learn new skills and strategies, and connect with other gamers and enthusiasts using the 35 gaming PCs and 4 console stations. The lab supports the NC State Esports program and serves as an incubator for esports research, teaching, learning and student involvement. Esports are electronic sports that involve playing video games, often at a high skill level. Many games involve intricate teamwork, and gameplay can be broadcast through livestreams on the web. Around the world, esports have a huge fan base and are a key part of the ever-growing gaming industry. At the lab, you can: Play or watch some of the most popular esports games, such as League of Legends, Counter-Strike, Dota 2, and Overwatch Access high-end gaming PCs with monitors and accessories optimized for competition Check out controllers and games to play on PlayStation, XBox, or Nintendo Switch stations Explore our gaming and esports workshops in areas such as game design, live streaming, getting started with gaming, and esports basics The lab is open to NC State students, faculty, and staff who are interested in gaming at any level of experience or playstyle. The Lenovo Esports & Gaming Lab is a place where you can have fun, learn, and belong. Complete our online orientation to gain access to the space! The lab is staffed whenever it is open, meaning you can find drop-in consultation assistance for projects, technology, and more just by stopping by. We're adding games over time! See our current games list.

photo.alt: Room full of gaming workstations and happy students, and video games on big screens

spaces.title: Maker Studio
spaces.description: Know before you go: our updated guidelines First-time users: take the required safety orientation (online) before you visit. The Hunt Library's Maker Studio is located on the fourth floor. This space gives students, faculty, and staff hands-on access to the tools, technologies, and skills of making, including 3D printers, low fidelity prototyping supplies, electronics, sewing machines, and many other tools and materials. The Maker Studio is intended for learning, experimentation, and prototyping and not for mass production or commercial use. The Maker Studio is staffed whenever it is open, meaning you can find drop-in consultation assistance for projects, technology, and more just by stopping by.

Reservable spaces require an orientation, which can be completed online. The Media Spaces at Hunt are staffed whenever we are open. You can find drop-in consultation assistance for projects, technology, and more just by stopping by. spaces.title: Teaching and Visualization Lab
spaces.description: The Teaching and Visualization Lab is a black-box room that offers 217 degrees of immersive projection on one smooth, curved projection screen that measures 85 feet in length. The room can host a variety of events including: High-impact learning activities, such as immersive student-led presentations and digital poster sessions Technology-rich interactive instruction sessions Creative digital media exhibits Simultaneous display of multiple devices (up to 8) for collaboration and presentation Presentations of large-scale visualizations and simulations Research communication Reservation requests are reviewed and accepted based on the following criteria: NC State University affiliation Impact on teaching, learning, and community Utilization of the immersive technology If you are an instructor and would like to use this space as part of a course assignment or final presentations, please plan to bring your students in at least 2 times: once for an overview and another time for the presentations.

photo.alt: Architecture presentation: students in chairs with a student presenting in front of them

spaces.title: The Landing
spaces.description: The Landing is a versatile wellness space for the NC State community. Students can relax and connect with others through board games, Legos, craft materials, and a variety of other hands-on activities. Throughout the year there are various events, hosted in the room, centered around stress reduction, emotional regulation, and mindfulness. When not reserved for specific events, The Landing is open for social gathering and group work. The room is equipped with plants, different light settings, and lounge seating. The room’s maximum capacity is 20. NC State University students, faculty, and staff can request to reserve The Landing for: Wellness activities Student-focused workshops and activities Scholarly sessions Campus initiatives related to student wellness Looking for gaming? Check out the Lenovo Esports and Gaming Lab .

spaces.title: VR Room
spaces.description: The VR Room is a reservable library space on the fourth floor of the James B. Hunt Jr. Library. This space is built for the exploration of spatial computing concepts through augmented and virtual reality. It's also a great location to record and edit audio or video, especially of gameplay or development. T his immersive studio space is designed for creators, developers, and explorers. Use the Meta Quest 3 or take advantage of our live capture tech, complete with background keying for high-quality visuals. Complete the Studios Orientation and reserve a time through our booking system to experience this fascinating equipment! Technology Our " What's Inside " section lists all of the technology that you'll find in the VR Room. Have a request for a piece of software or hardware you'd like to see in the VR Room? Let us know with as much information on the item as possible. Need help? Schedule a technology consultation with us! The Studios Check out our full suite of services, spaces, and expert help . Looking for Gaming and VR at the Hill Library? Check out the Gaming & VR Studio .
